The package existing eSIM operators onboard with: the seller node AI agents buy from over x402, a neutral supplier interface with ready adapters (eSIM Access, Airalo, eSIM Go, and HTTP for your own system), signed webhooks for your CRM and billing, the `esim.*@v1` JSON Schemas and the conformance check `esim-rails check`. Reference: SDK · integrations · onboarding; setup of the whole kit: operator guide; calling it: agent guide. Open rails for selling travel data eSIMs through an AIMarket hub. Anyone with a wholesale account runs a seller node; buyers — AI agents booking trips, apps, a storefront for travellers — find the cheapest plan across every connected seller and buy it with one x402 payment. The hub routes and takes its routing fee; the seller is the merchant (its prices, its VAT, its refunds). Status: v0.1. The wholesale client, offers, pricing, the order flow and the seller node (free signed quote and status, the paid order behind x402) are written and tested. A live test order (2026-10-14) went through `fulfil`, `status` and `release` against eSIM Access: the cheapest plan ($0.30) was allocated in about 2.5 s, the same payment sent again found the same profile, a wrong status token was refused, and the cancelled profile's price returned to the balance. ## The three capabilities Capability | Price | Input | Answer --- | --- | --- | --- `esim.quote@v1` | free | `country` (ISO alpha-2), optional `min_gb`, `min_days`, `max_usd`, `limit` | offers covering the country, cheapest first — regional and global plans that include it count `esim.order@v1` | the offer's price, x402 (USDC on Base) | `offer_id` | `activation_code` (the LPA string an eSIM is installed from), `qr_code_url`, `install_url`, `iccid`, `apn`, `expires`, `status_token` `esim.status@v1` | free | `esim_tran_no`, `status_token` | state, installed or not, data used and total, expiry — and the activation code again An offer (`src/offers.js`) reads the same whichever wholesaler is behind it: `offer_id`, `name`, `coverage {kind, countries}`, `data_bytes`, `data_gb`, `days`, `speed`, `networks`, `top_up`, `unused_valid_days`, `price {usd, currency}`, `usd_per_gb`. The wholesale cost never leaves the node. Ask with `min_gb` and `min_days`: without them the cheapest offer is often a 0.1 GB plan. `scripts/catalog.mjs` shows a seller what it would sell, read-only: balance, plan count, the shape of the supplier's fields, and the top offers for a few countries at its margin. The first live read (2026-10-14) found 1 728 fixed plans, all with a slug, all USD and days; e.g. France 1 GB / 7 days at $0.70 wholesale. ## What the order flow guarantees (`src/order.js`) * One payment, one profile. The wholesaler's `transactionId` is derived from the payment, and the supplier treats a repeated id as the same order: a retry after a lost answer cannot buy twice. * The activation code goes to the payer only. It is in the answer and nowhere else — not in the node's store (a test reads the file), not in logs, not in any receipt or feed. The payer gets a `status_token` (an HMAC of the profile number under the node's secret) to read the profile again. * Delivered, then settled. The node verifies the payment, orders, waits for the profile (the supplier allocated the test order's in 2.5 s; the node waits up to 45 s), and settles only after that. A refused order buys nothing; an allocation that is still running is reported and resumes on retry with the same payment; a payment that fails to settle cancels the profile, which the supplier refunds while it is unused. * The price is checked twice. The order carries the wholesale price the offer was quoted at, so a plan whose price changed since the quote is refused by the supplier rather than charged. ## Suppliers * eSIM Access (`src/esimaccess.js`): signed requests (`RT-AccessCode`, `RT-RequestID`, `RT-Timestamp`, `RT-Signature` = HMAC-SHA256 of timestamp + request id + access code + body under the secret key — the supplier's own test vector is in the tests), prices in 1/10 000 USD, 8 requests a second, no sandbox (a test order is cancelled and refunded). Keys are read from files and never logged, returned or sent anywhere but the supplier's host. * Next: eSIM Go, Airalo Partners — each is one more client behind the same offers and order flow. ## The node (`src/node.js`, `src/server.js`) Route | --- | --- `POST /quote/invoke`, `POST /status/invoke` | the hub's provider contract: `{success, result}` with an Ed25519 `X-Provider-Signature` over the request-bound canonical the hub verifies `POST /order` | `{offer_id}` — an unknown offer is a 400 before any price; then the x402 paywall (`src/paywall.js`: CDP facilitator, USDC on Base, the offer's price read from the request, paid to `PAY_TO`); the answer is released only after settlement `GET /listing.json` | the two hub listings and where the order is bought `GET /healthz` | catalogue loaded, provider key, whether orders are on Configuration is in `src/server.js` (keys as files; the status secret and the provider key are made on first start). Without `PAY_TO` and `CDP_KEY_FILE` the node quotes but takes no orders. ## Connecting as a seller The kit's `docker-compose.yml` runs this node behind Caddy at `https:///agents/`, beside the storefront and the federation node. The operator guide covers the wholesale account ($50 first top-up), the keys, the CDP key for x402, `node.toml` and the test order. `deploy.sh` is how modelmarket.dev runs its demo node (`DEMO_MODE=1`: quotes, no orders). Selling to consumers makes you the merchant: in the EU that means VAT on telecom services in the buyer's country (OSS). The rails do not hold anyone's money. ## Test `npm test # node:test, no network, no keys ` ## Keywords esim x402 ai-agents aimarket travel usdc +3 more FAQs What is @aimarket/esim-rails? An agent can build and deploy an application. This kit lets it take the next step: obtain a signed price for a domain, register it to its real owner, manage DNS and connect it to a Vercel project. Independent operators run their own seller nodes, use their own registrar accounts and set a **fixed markup per registration or renewal**. Agents use a shared capability contract and a budgeted MCP client. > **Pre-live release.** The local tests and Openprovider and Porkbun Sandbox pilots pass: registration, DNS, renewal, lost-response recovery and MCP reads. Production domain purchases, payment settlement and Vercel attachment remain unverified. The default demo buys nothing. [Verification record →](VALIDATION.md) ## What the buyer gets **One exact domain, registered for one year to the supplied registrant.** The quote shows the supplier cost, fixed markup and final amount before payment. For example, a $10 supplier cost plus a $2 markup gives a 12 USDC order; these are illustrative amounts, not a registrar tariff. DNS management and domain information are included. Renewal is a separate purchase at a newly quoted price. Registrar autorenew is disabled. Availability is not a reservation, and registrant email verification may still require action by the owner. The built-in registrar scope is `.com`, `.net` and `.org`, ordinary ASCII names, one year. Premium names, IDNs, incoming transfers and expired-domain restoration are outside this release. ## One product, three roles | You are | What you use | |---|---| | **A domain operator or reseller** | Your registrar account, receiving wallet, refund reserve and fixed markup; a seller node with durable orders | | **An independent supplier** | The [HTTP supplier contract](SUPPLIERS.md), implemented in your own language and infrastructure | | **An agent or app developer** | Signed `domains.*@v1` capabilities, the JavaScript client or the [stdio MCP configuration](examples/mcp.json) | ```mermaid flowchart LR Agent["AI agent / MCP client"] -->|Discover| Hub["AIMarket Hub"] Hub -->|Public quotes only| Seller["Domain operator"] Agent -->|Private order + x402 payment| Seller Seller -->|Register and reconcile| Provider["Openprovider / Porkbun / HTTP supplier"] Agent -->|Owner-signed DNS| Seller Agent -->|Buyer-side connector| Vercel["Your Vercel project"] ``` The Hub handles discovery. Orders, registrant contacts, payment authorizations and DNS operations go directly to the seller. This implementation charges no Hub commission. The Vercel token stays with the buyer. ## Try it locally Use Node.js **22.13+**; local verification used **22.22.1**. From `domain-kit/` in the monorepo, or from the root of a satellite checkout: ```sh npm ci --ignore-scripts npm run check npm test npm run demo ``` The demo runs a signed HTTP lifecycle: **quote → simulated registration → DNS → renewal**. No registrar account, wallet funding or external service is needed. Local HTTP tests require permission to listen on localhost. For the simplest external API test, use the [Porkbun Sandbox quickstart](PORKBUN.md): automatic disposable credentials, virtual credit and a resumable end-to-end pilot. The Porkbun adapter is sandbox-only until a production pilot passes. For the Openprovider Sandbox API integration test, follow the opt-in [`npm run sandbox:pilot` instructions](PILOT.md#повторяемый-sandbox-пилот). The script retains its state and reuses the same orders on repeat runs. For a persistent demo server: ```sh cp .env.example .env node --env-file=.env src/server.js ``` In another terminal: ```sh DOMAIN_ALLOW_DEMO=1 node bin/domain-rails.mjs check http://127.0.0.1:9495 ``` This checks the public quote protocol and signature; it does not certify the seller. The server persists encrypted documents and keys in `data/`. Do not discard that directory between deployments. ### A public node: demo until your keys are in `DOMAIN_MODE=auto` is for a node you publish before you sell. Without keys it is a **public demo**: availability is real (the registries' own RDAP for `.com`, `.net`, `.org`), quotes are signed and marked `demo` with illustrative prices, reads answer, and only `register` and `renew` are refused with `403 demo_mode`.
